page_title: compression.zstd — Compression compatible with the Zstandard format

sources.entry: compression.zstd - (Python standard library) Compress and decompress data in the Zstandard format.

summary.name: compression.zstd
summary.one_liner: Python standard library module (added in 3.14) for compressing and decompressing data and .zst files in the Zstandard format.
use_cases: Compress or decompress bytes in memory with Python
Read and write .zst files from Python code
Compress many small similar files using a trained Zstandard dictionary
Incrementally compress or decompress streamed data
Tune compression ratio and speed with advanced parameters
summary.what_it_does: The module provides open() and the ZstdFile class for reading and writing Zstandard-compressed files in binary or text mode, including .zst files made by the zstd utility. It offers one-shot compress() and decompress() functions, plus ZstdCompressor and ZstdDecompressor objects for incremental work. Zstandard dictionaries can be trained from sample data with train_dict(), finalized with finalize_dict(), and wrapped in the ZstdDict class to improve compression of small, similar data. Advanced tuning is available through the CompressionParameter, DecompressionParameter, and Strategy classes.
notable: Part of the Python standard library since version 3.14, listed in awesome-python under File Manipulation
Supports Zstandard dictionary training and finalization for small-data compression
Reads multi-frame input via decompress() and ZstdFile; ZstdDecompressor handles only single frames
caveats: It is an optional module; if missing from a CPython build, the distributor's documentation must be consulted
ZstdDecompressor does not transparently handle inputs with multiple compressed frames
Passing level and options together is not allowed; when reading, passing level raises TypeError
